facts.fact: The shim pack stacking order is critical and cannot be inverted. AUTHORITATIVE order (per the CORRECT_Order reference video): thick washer (cod.92203637) down first, then shims, then thin washer (cod.191713A1) on top. NOTE: this operator's audio described the reverse sequence ('thin washer, shims, thick washer') — that mismatch is exactly the kind of mix-up this check guards against; always defer to the correct-order reference.

citation.transcript_quote: thin washer, uh shims and the thick washer. It cannot be inverted or anything.

facts.fact: New workers and cross-training operators are the most likely to mix up the shim pack stacking sequence, and have historically asked the experienced operator to confirm the correct order.
facts.applies_when: when a new or cross-training worker is performing the step

citation.transcript_quote: whenever a new worker or somebody's cross training, I think there is a chance that it can happen

facts.fact: The target rolling torque that the shim pack must achieve is approximately 5.6 to 20.3 Newton meters.

citation.transcript_quote: around 5.6 to 20.3 Newton meters of rolling torque

facts.fact: Selecting the correct total shim pack thickness to hit the rolling-torque specification is a trial-and-error process that may require the operator to repeat the measurement and adjustment multiple times.

citation.transcript_quote: they might have to repeat it again and again because this… it's trial and error

facts.fact: The thin spacer and thick spacer look very similar (difference is mainly thickness), making them easy to confuse; visual inspection alone may not reliably distinguish them.

citation.transcript_quote: I mean it's just the difference, I think, the thickness… it's too similar
